issues.description: Frame carries a live FrameProcessor reference, conflating value with mutable runtime identity
issues.detail: ServiceSwitcherRequestMetadataFrame.service holds a FrameProcessor instance instead of a stable identifier. Control frames are value-like; embedding a processor reference risks serialization breakage, GC retention of swapped-out services, and equality surprises. A service name or id would preserve the targeting invariant without coupling the frame to object lifetime.

issues.description: Targeting uses default object equality on FrameProcessor without stating the invariant
issues.detail: The suppression check `frame.service == self.strategy.active_service` relies on inherited identity-based __eq__. If a subclass overrides equality, or the active service is wrapped/replaced, the switcher silently stops suppressing and the control frame leaks downstream. Use `is`, a stable id, and document the invariant explicitly.

issues.description: Push-after-handle protocol and non-active-target behavior are unspecified
issues.detail: STTService and the mock now handle metadata then re-push the frame, expecting the switcher to swallow it on match. The ordering invariant, the responsibility split, and behavior when a frame targets an inactive service are nowhere stated. A future refactor reversing order or broadcasting will silently break correctness. Document and test all cases.

issues.description: Forward-reference type "FrameProcessor" is unresolved in frames.py
issues.detail: The dataclass field is annotated as the string "FrameProcessor" but the symbol is not imported in frames.py. Runtime construction works, but get_type_hints, dataclass introspection, serializers, and IDE tooling will fail to resolve it. Either add a TYPE_CHECKING import or use a stable id field with an honest type.

issues.description: Test asserts frame presence but not the targeting invariant
issues.detail: The updated test checks that service2 received one ServiceSwitcherRequestMetadataFrame but never asserts `request_frames[0].service is service2`. The rename's whole point is targeted dispatch; the test proves frames arrive, not that the target field is correct. Add an assertion on the service field.

synthesis.summary: The panel converges strongly: the rename is a real clarity win, but the implementation embeds a live FrameProcessor reference inside a value-like control frame, complecting data with mutable runtime identity. Targeting then leans on default object equality without stating the invariant, and the new handle-then-re-push protocol splits responsibility between service and switcher without documenting the ordering or the non-active-target case. A stable service id, a single point of consumption, and explicit invariants would resolve the design concern. Tests confirm frames arrive but never assert the target field is correct.
